english: Children are not allowed to watch this movie.
tip: нельзя (nelzya = not allowed) puts the person in the dative: Детям нельзя (Detyam nelzya = children may not). There is no verb 'to be'.

target: Рад познакомиться с вами наконец лично.
english: I'm pleased to finally meet you in person.
tip: с (s) means 'with' and takes the instrumental: с вами (s vami = with you). The verb познакомиться (poznakomitsya = get acquainted) always pairs with с.

target: Они посадили молодое дерево в саду.
english: They planted a young tree in the garden.
tip: A few masculine nouns take a stressed -у in the locative: в саду (v sadu = in the garden), not в саде (v sade). Same for в лесу (v lesu), на мосту (na mostu).

target: Продавец редко играет в шахматы после работы.
english: The salesman rarely plays chess after work.
tip: For games, use играть в (igrat v = play) plus the accusative: играет в шахматы (igrayet v shakhmaty = plays chess). Instruments take играть на (igrat na).

english: Besides you, nobody came.
tip: кроме (krome = besides) takes the genitive: кроме тебя (krome tebya = besides you).

english: He went out of the house.
tip: из (iz = out of) takes the genitive and matches the вы- (vy-) prefix: вышел из дома (vyshel iz doma = went out of the house).

english: He came up to the window.
tip: к (k = toward) takes the dative: подошёл к окну (podoshyol k oknu = came up to the window).

english: Because of the rain we stayed home.
tip: из-за (iz-za = because of) takes the genitive and marks a negative cause: из-за дождя (iz-za dozhdya = because of the rain).

english: The dog needs a walk every day.
tip: нужен (nuzhen) agrees with the needed noun, not the person: прогулка (progulka, feminine) takes нужна (nuzhna = is needed).

english: The cat likes to sleep in the sun.
tip: The one who likes goes dative: коту (kotu = to the cat). The verb agrees with the liked thing: нравится (nravitsya = likes, singular).

target: Она стала учительницей два года назад.
english: She became a teacher two years ago.
tip: стать (stat' = to become) takes the instrumental: стала учительницей (stala uchitel'nitsey = became a teacher).

english: Friends always help each other.
tip: друг другу (drug drugu = each other) is fixed; only the second word shifts case, here dative after помогают (pomogayut = help).

english: It's difficult for me to speak Russian.
tip: Difficulty puts the person in the dative with no subject 'it': мне трудно (mne trudno = it is hard for me).

english: Russian winter can be very cold.
tip: бывает (byvaet = tends to be) marks a recurring trait and takes an instrumental complement: холодной (kholodnoy = cold).

english: I have nothing to wear to the party.
tip: нечего (nechego) plus an infinitive means having nothing to: нечего надеть (nechego nadet' = nothing to wear); the person goes dative, мне (mne).

english: The table stands in the center of the room.
tip: Russian places things with posture verbs: стол стоит (stol stoit = the table stands), not a plain 'is'.

target: Между друзьями не должно быть секретов.
english: There should be no secrets between friends.
tip: между (mezhdu = between) takes the instrumental: между друзьями (mezhdu druz'yami = between friends).

english: Among the guests were famous artists.
tip: среди (sredi = among) takes the genitive: среди гостей (sredi gostey = among the guests).

target: Букет из красных роз стоит в вазе.
english: A bouquet of red roses is in the vase.
tip: из also means made of, with the genitive: букет из роз (buket iz roz = a bouquet of roses).

english: She gave flowers to mom.
tip: The receiver goes in the dative: маме (mame = to mom). The gift цветы (tsvety = flowers) stays the direct object.

english: He became a famous doctor.
tip: After стал (stal = became), the new role goes in the instrumental: известным врачом (izvestnym vrachom = a famous doctor).

english: We are proud of our children.
tip: The verb гордимся (gordimsya = we are proud) takes the instrumental with no preposition: нашими детьми (nashimi det'mi = our children).

english: Mushroom soup smells wonderful.
tip: с (s = with) takes the instrumental: с грибами (s gribami = with mushrooms), naming what the soup is made with.

english: She told about her childhood.
tip: о (o = about) takes the prepositional case: о своём детстве (o svoyom detstve = about her childhood).

english: A doctor's work requires great patience.
tip: требует (trebuyet = requires) takes the genitive, not the accusative: большого терпения (bol'shogo terpeniya = great patience).

english: A sturdy table stands in the corner.
tip: This masculine noun takes a stressed -у for location: в углу (v uglu = in the corner), not the usual -е ending.

english: Behind the fence there is a big garden.
tip: за (za = behind) takes the instrumental for a static location: за забором (za zaborom = behind the fence).

target: Мальчику подарили велосипед на день рождения.
english: The boy was given a bicycle for his birthday.
tip: With no stated subject, the plural verb подарили (podarili = they gave) reads as a passive, was given, the normal Russian pattern.

english: Colleagues liked my presentation.
tip: понравилась (ponravilas', feminine) agrees with презентация (prezentatsiya = presentation), the thing liked, not with коллегам (kollegam = colleagues).

english: The boy eats soup with a spoon.
tip: The tool used takes the instrumental with no preposition: ложкой (lozhkoy = with a spoon).
